nodes.label: Source hierarchy: cahier V2 > Projet Complet > claude.md
TGFT platform
nodes.rationale: Evaluated on architecture, not features: minimal core + per-group modules + open marketplace.

nodes.label: Noyau minimal (accounts, groups, members, roles, permissions)
Marketplace ouverte
nodes.rationale: Primary value is the constraint it imposes on the developer: all features go through public contracts, preventing drift into an accidental monolith.

nodes.label: Shared module contracts (manifest, activation, role permissions, purge/anonymisation)
nodes.rationale: Native and external modules share the exact same contracts; only execution differs. Guard against purely decorative extensibility.

nodes.label: Team Builder module (MVP)
nodes.rationale: Chosen for technical richness and visual demo value.

nodes.label: Versioned board state encoding in URL
nodes.rationale: Link is the shared object, nothing stored; game IDs change every set (~4 months) so encoding must be versioned for old links to stay interpretable.

nodes.label: Tier Lists module (MVP)
nodes.rationale: Cheapest module in the catalog; enough to establish plurality of native modules.

nodes.label: Contributor has no rights on members or modules (C7, C8)
nodes.rationale: Formulated negatively on purpose; verified by authorization tests across all endpoints, not by a screen.

nodes.label: Structural multi-tenant isolation (C10)
nodes.rationale: Never rely on per-query manual filters: a single omission suffices and is silent.

nodes.label: Hosting budget < 10 EUR/month, single x86 VPS
nodes.rationale: Structurally excludes container or database per group/module.

nodes.label: Classeur (per-module, per-group SQLite file)
nodes.rationale: Chosen by platform, never module; size-capped; module never writes SQL.

nodes.label: Module call flow (event, preparation, execution, verification)
nodes.rationale: Calls of one module for one group are serialized: no concurrent classeur writes.

nodes.label: No host functions during execution (closed box)
nodes.rationale: Each question a module could ask is another door to guard; giving everything up front means only the response must be checked.

nodes.label: Salle des machines (isolated Wasm execution service)
nodes.rationale: Separate Docker container, no secrets, no outbound network, no DB, read-only FS; an escaping module finds nothing exploitable.

nodes.label: 8 independent protection layers
nodes.rationale: Layers are independent: failure of one does not compromise the system.

nodes.label: WebAssembly sandbox with fuel and memory caps
Wasmtime for .NET 48 (LTS)
nodes.rationale: Bytecode Alliance engine built for untrusted code, public CVE process, LTS = 24 months of security fixes, official .NET library. Ops rules after April 2026 CVEs: x86 server, default compiler, fast security updates.

nodes.label: Javy (JS -> Wasm compiler)
nodes.rationale: JS engine compiled into the module so engine defects stay confined; JS lowers the entry barrier.

nodes.label: Jint fallback plan
nodes.rationale: If Javy+Wasmtime prototype fails, switch to Jint (C# JS interpreter) in the same isolated machine room; layer 2 becomes main protection; everything else unchanged.

nodes.label: Q6: end-to-end Javy + Wasmtime prototype (first milestone)
SQLite (Microsoft.Data.Sqlite)
nodes.rationale: Physical data separation, purge by file deletion, size quota, no extra server.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL (RLS, JSONB)
nodes.rationale: RLS is a second wall independent of app code; JSONB suits variable module config schemas; stores user<->pseudonym mapping out of module reach.

nodes.label: EF Core global query filters + Dapper
nodes.rationale: Filters declared once per entity apply to all queries, making isolation structural rather than declarative.

nodes.label: Per-module pseudonyms (M12)
nodes.rationale: Prevents a module from tracking a member across modules.

nodes.label: Declarative UI (no third-party code in browser)
Trust levels + global kill switch (M5, M7)
Tests are the security mechanism
nodes.rationale: Isolation, architecture and hostile-suite tests are the protection itself; blocking in CI; never disable or bypass.

nodes.label: External module lifecycle (write, compile, publish, activate, run, retire)
Attested compilation from public repo via GitHub Actions (M4, P2)
nodes.rationale: P2 without weakening security: sandbox protects identically; only code-origin traceability is deferred.

nodes.label: RGPD purge (B8) and anonymisation (A5) by architecture
nodes.rationale: Purge = delete classeurs; anonymise = delete pseudonym mapping. Free text not covered, so publication rules forbid soliciting personal data.

nodes.label: D11: native modules implement anonymisation + purge, compile-time checked
nodes.rationale: Conditions A4, A5, B8; must be in place before the first module since it cannot be retrofitted.

nodes.label: B8: delete group and all its data (MVP)
nodes.rationale: Only story that actually exercises D11 and M13 purge; a guarantee never exercised is a guarantee not owned.

nodes.label: Clean Architecture (Domain / Application / Infrastructure / Api)
nodes.rationale: Split Domain and Application so the Javy->Jint switch touches only Infrastructure, and NetArchTest can assert Domain references nothing (D8).

nodes.label: Testcontainers (real disposable DB for isolation tests)
ASP.NET Core (C#) back-end
nodes.rationale: Bot and machine room in the same language share compile-checked data contracts.

nodes.label: Angular front-end (lazy-loaded per module)
nodes.rationale: Lazy loading aligned with modularity: an inactive module costs nothing; renders external module screens with platform components.

nodes.label: Caddy reverse proxy
nodes.rationale: Single public entry; API never directly exposed; handles HTTPS certs and serves Angular statics (hence no SSR).

nodes.label: In-memory + disk cache, no Redis
nodes.rationale: Redis only helps multi-instance deployment, not the chosen model. Board images named by content hash + game version.

nodes.label: Data Dragon (Riot static game data)
nodes.rationale: No API key needed, no revocation risk; checked daily.

nodes.label: L4: bot commands match group's activated modules
nodes.rationale: Most structuring bot story: forces modules to declare commands in their manifest; proof modularity spans the whole platform.

nodes.label: Discord for external modules (P3, DeferAsync, mentions disabled)
AGPL-3.0 + DCO licensing
nodes.rationale: Network clause covers modified software offered as a service. External modules must be public under an OSI license (also enables M4).

nodes.label: Riot Games legal framework
nodes.rationale: Non-commercial, 'not endorsed by Riot' notice, no game client interaction, no official ranking estimation; applies to external modules too.

nodes.label: Settled decisions (no DLL modules, no container per module, no Rust/WIT/ComponentizeJS, no Extism, no Redis)
nodes.rationale: .NET has no in-process isolation (CAS removed); budget; experimental tools; Extism .NET not patched.
